name: IAI 1124 Westwind
summary: IAI's turbofan-powered development of the Aero Commander Jet Commander (1963), a rugged older business jet with distinctive wingtip tanks.

wings: Low, slightly swept wing with large, long wingtip fuel tanks
engines: Two Garrett TFE731 turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Slim, round fuselage with a row of oval windows
tail: Swept fin with a low-set horizontal stabilizer on the rear fuselage (not a T-tail)

tellTales: Long cylindrical tip tanks on the ends of the wings
Low-set tailplane on a swept fin, with rear engine pods
Slim body with a row of oval windows

confusedWith.howToTell: The Learjet 35 has a T-tail and a smaller, narrower fuselage; the Westwind has a low-set tailplane and a slightly larger body.
The Astra/G150 has a T-tail and no tip tanks; the Westwind has tip tanks and a low-set tailplane.
The Falcon 20 has small round windows and plain wingtips; the Westwind has oval windows and large tip tanks.
The Learjet 24/25 is smaller with a T-tail and small turbojet pods; the Westwind is larger with a low-set tailplane.
